title: Comparative synthesis: shadow run and regression triage (Jun 2028)
content:
Purpose and context:
This note summarizes the June 2028 shadow-run comparison across three onboarding candidates and the current prod baseline. The goal: synthesize model-level wins/losses across our canonical prompt suites, identify regression signals, and define a safe canary + rollback plan. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — rapid triage output for PM/SE/ops alignment.

Quick executive summary:
- Candidates evaluated: cand-a-3.1-fp16, cand-b-3.2-int8, cand-c-3.2-quant (mixed precision + KV cache tweaks). Baseline: prod-2028-05 (redwood-v1).
- Primary signal: instruction-following score (IFS) aggregated over 12 prompt cohorts. Secondary signals: semantic-quality (human eval proxy), latency p50/p95, tokens-per-second (TPS), and cost multiplier.
- Winner by composite leaderboard: cand-c-3.2-quant (composite score 0.87 vs baseline 0.76). Cand-b close on latency/cost but small regressions on safe-instruction follow. Cand-a beat baseline on QA but lost on code-generation tests.
- Regression flags: two prompt cohorts (legal-advice and medical-summary) show significant IFS drop for cand-b (delta -4.3% absolute; bootstrap p<0.01). Cand-c shows minor safety drift in hallucination rate on lists-of-facts (delta +1.6% but not statistically significant at our threshold).
- Recommendation: Promote cand-c-3.2-quant to limited canary (5% production traffic for 48h with shadow logging and roll-forward/rollback hooks). Require additional prompt-specific calibration for legal/medical cohorts before broader rollout.

Evaluation setup (short):
- Datasets: master_promptset_v3 (12 cohorts: general-qa, summarization-long, summarization-short, instruction-follow, code-gen, math, extraction, safety-probes, conversation, creative, legal, medical).
- Metrics: Instruction-following score (IFS, auto + sampled human check), win-rate (pairwise head-to-head), semanticBLEU (approx), latency p50/p95, TPS, cost-multiplier (inference tokens * model_cost_coeff).
- Human eval: 600 sampled pairs across cohorts (blind A/B, 3 raters per sample).
- Statistical testing: bootstrap CI (1000 resamples) for delta IFS; significance threshold p<0.05 but we use p<0.01 for regression alarms.
- Shadow run config: 10k requests per candidate (balanced across cohorts), KV cache warmup enabled where applicable, typical seq len distribution sampled from live telemetry (median 128, 95th 640).

Composite leaderboard (top 5 snippets):
1) cand-c-3.2-quant — composite 0.87 (IFS +0.09 vs baseline, semanticBLEU +0.06, latency p50 +12ms)
2) cand-b-3.2-int8 — composite 0.82 (IFS -0.02, latency p50 -18ms, cost -22%)
3) cand-a-3.1-fp16 — composite 0.79 (IFS +0.01, code-gen +0.07, latency p50 +30ms)
4) prod-2028-05 (baseline) — composite 0.76
5) experimental-mini-3 — composite 0.64 (excluded from consideration)

Pairwise win/loss highlights (aggregated across cohorts):
- cand-c vs baseline: head-to-head win-rate 62% weighted by cohort importance; net wins strongest on long-form summarization and extraction; minor losses on safety probes.
- cand-b vs baseline: win-rate 49% (statistically tie), strong latency/cost wins but regression on legal and medical prompt cohorts.
- cand-a vs baseline: win-rate 54% but high variance by task; best on code-gen, worse on long conversations.

Regression triage details (critical):
- Legal cohort regression (cand-b): absolute IFS drop -4.3%; human-rated harmful/incorrect legal guidance occurrences increased from 1.2% -> 4.6%. Likely cause: int8 quantization + prune on some attention kernels observed to drop precision on rare-token patterns (case law citations). Action: block cand-b from legal/medical routes until a targeted prompt calibration and kernel tuning patch (PR 412) is applied.
- Medical cohort (cand-b): similar shape to legal; risk unacceptable for regulated customers.
- Hallucination bump (cand-c): +1.6% on list-of-facts probes; appears concentrated on long context token sequences >512 when KV compression heuristic triggers. Not urgent but monitor.

Detailed per-cohort notes (short bullets):
- General QA: all candidates improved median correctness; cand-c highest semantic score.
- Long summarization: cand-c superior (better coherence at 2-3 paragraph scale).
- Short summarization: tie across candidates.
- Code generation: cand-a leads on compilation-success proxy; cand-c close but slightly more extraneous comments.
- Math: baseline still best on exact arithmetic tasks (cand-c slight regression on precision for 64-bit integer ops).
- Safety probes: cand-b regressed on two prompt families; cand-c slight uptick but below alarm threshold.
- Conversation: cand-c better at persona consistency; cand-a sometimes repeats system token fragments.

Operational metrics and cost tradeoffs:
- Latency p50 (ms): baseline 78; cand-b 60; cand-c 90; cand-a 108.
- Latency p95 (ms): baseline 210; cand-b 170; cand-c 225; cand-a 320.
- TPS (tokens/sec): cand-b +28% vs baseline; cand-c +5%; cand-a -10%.
- Cost multiplier (per-token): cand-b 0.78x; cand-c 0.92x; cand-a 1.05x.

Decision rationale and recommended rollout:
1) Promote cand-c-3.2-quant to canary (5% traffic) for 48 hours with the following constraints:
  - Exclude legal and medical routes from canary traffic until targeted calibration is applied.
  - Enable full shadow logging (request+response diffs, KV cache hit traces) and increase human-eval sampling for safety cohorts (daily 150 pairs).
  - Add automated regression alarms: IFS drop >1.5% on any cohort sustained for 3 reporting windows (1h windows) or hallucination rate +2% absolute.
2) Do NOT promote cand-b to production at this time due to legal/medical regressions despite attractive latency/cost. Prioritize kernel/quant fixes and re-run only when regression tests pass.
3) Keep cand-a in the experimental track; interesting for code-gen customers but not general-purpose prod.

Rollback criteria (explicit):
- Immediate rollback if any of the following occur during canary:
  - IFS for any cohort drops more than 2% absolute vs baseline in a 1-hour window (with p<0.05 on bootstrap).
  - Hallucination rate for safety probes increases >2.5% absolute and confirmed by human sample.
  - Error rate (5xx/timeout) increases >1% absolute.

Follow-ups and action items (owners + ETA):
- SE: implement cohort exclusion filter for canary routing (Ethan Kim) — ETA 2028-06-20.
- Applied ML: run targeted prompt calibration for legal/medical with 3-shot anchors; retest cand-b after kernel patch (Sofia Ramirez) — ETA 2028-06-25.
- Runtime: add KV-compression debug logging for cand-c during canary (Liam O'Connor) — ETA 2028-06-19.
- PM: schedule 30-min roll decision sync after 24h of canary data (Ava Patel) — ETA daily cadence while canary active.

Notes on eval limitations and caveats:
- Sample sizes for some niche cohorts (legal subsections: tax vs family law) are small — treat those deltas as noisy until we expand sample.
- Our human eval panel is partially overlapping with annotators used in earlier bakeoffs which may bias towards baseline phrasing; will recruit 20% fresh raters next run.
- Cost multipliers are modeled; live infra billing may differ under sustained heavy concurrency.

Appendix (short):
- Raw leaderboard CSV uploaded to GH PR 412 (link above).
- Quick diffs: example long-summary from baseline vs cand-c (attached in GH PR comment).
- Slack thread: #aml-shadow-run Jun 12-14 for granular logs.

If you disagree with the recommended canary or see missed edge-cases, add comments inline and flag during the roll decision sync.

-- end of note --
